question: Should OpenClaw add a target-agent subagent concurrency budget, and should it compose as min(global subagent cap, target-agent cap) for both native and ACP spawns?
rationale: This adds public configuration and scheduling policy; source inspection establishes the gap but cannot choose the permanent config namespace or fairness semantics.

options.title: Add hierarchical target cap
options.body: Add agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent and enforce it alongside the shared global pool for every sessions_spawn runtime.

options.title: Use named lanes instead
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/10467 the canonical design and require callers or configuration to route work through explicit named concurrency lanes.

options.title: Keep global-only limits
options.body: Decline another config surface and retain the current shared global and per-requester safety limits.

recommendation.title: Add hierarchical target cap
recommendation.body: Add agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent and enforce it alongside the shared global pool for every sessions_spawn runtime.

likelyOwner.reason: They are connected to the central concurrency resolver history and have already provided product-oriented follow-up on this issue.
